content: The pharmacokinetics of albendazole and praziquantel were studied in Thai children infected with Giardia intestinalis. This research was published in Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 2004, volume 98, pages 349–357. Dexamethasone has been shown to increase plasma levels of albendazole. This finding was reported in the Journal of Neurology in 1990, volume 237, pages 279–280. The interaction between albendazole sulfoxide and dexamethasone in the treatment of neurocysticercosis was explored, highlighting pharmacokinetic considerations. This study appeared in Therapeutic Drug Monitoring in 1997, volume 19, pages 51–55. Praziquantel has been evaluated for its safety and efficacy in treating schistosomiasis during pregnancy. This was documented in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2018, volume 96, pages 59–65. The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed guidelines for the control and elimination of schistosomiasis, with a forthcoming update expected in 2021. The European Medicines Agency (EMA) has provided a summary report on albendazole, including its extrapolation to all ruminants. This report was finalized in 2004 and is available online. A systematic review examined the effects of albendazole or mebendazole exposure during pregnancy, particularly in the first trimester, on maternal and child outcomes. This was published in the International Journal of Parasitology in 2019, volume 49, pages 541–554. Cases of neurocysticercosis identified at Sanglah Hospital in Bali, Indonesia, from 2014 to 2018 were reported in Acta Tropica in 2020, volume 201, article 105208. The systemic availability of albendazole increases when taken with a fatty meal, as demonstrated in a study published in the European Journal of Clinical Pharmacology in 1988, volume 34, pages 315–317. The influence of a traditional Mexican diet on the bioavailability of albendazole was investigated and published in Basic & Clinical Pharmacology & Toxicology in 2005, volume 97, pages 122–124. The bioavailability of praziquantel increases when administered with food, as reported in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2000, volume 44, pages 2903–2904. The co-administration of grapefruit juice or cimetidine with albendazole affects its bioavailability. This was detailed in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2002, volume 66, pages 260–263. The interaction between grapefruit juice and praziquantel in humans was explored in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2002, volume 46, pages 1614–1616. The WHO has emphasized the importance of monitoring drug coverage for preventive chemotherapy in public health programs. This was outlined in a 2010 publication available online. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has developed tools for monitoring the coverage of integrated public health interventions, including vaccination and deworming for soil-transmitted helminthiasis. This was published in 2017 and is accessible online. Principles for justifying public health interventions were discussed in the Canadian Journal of Public Health in 2002, volume 93, pages 101–103. A review of international no-fault compensation programs for adverse events attributed to vaccination was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2011, volume 89, pages 371–378. Ethical and evidence-based considerations for investing in the eradication of lymphatic filariasis and onchocerciasis were discussed in the American Journal of Public Health in 2015, volume 105, pages 629–636. A study on deworming coverage and equity in lowand middle-income countries, using household health surveys, was published in The Lancet Global Health in 2019, volume 7, pages e1511–e1520. Neglected tropical diseases were examined as a measure of universal health coverage, with lessons from four country contexts. This was published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2019, volume 13, article e0007847. The WHO has highlighted the importance of pharmacovigilance as an essential tool for ensuring the safety of medicines in public health programs. This was detailed in a 2006 publication available online. The WHO has also promoted the safety of medicines for children, as outlined in a 2007 publication accessible online. Practical advice for managing serious adverse events in preventive chemotherapy programs for neglected tropical diseases was provided by the WHO in a 2011 publication available online. A handbook for managing adverse events following mass drug administration was developed by USAID, RTI International, and the Task Force for Global Health in 2015, and is available online. The impact of repeated mass drug administration with praziquantel and targeted treatment of taeniosis cases on the prevalence of Taenia solium in endemic rural communities in Tanzania was studied and published in Acta Tropica in 2017, volume 165, pages 246–251.
